# Kathinakkhandhaka (Kd 7)

**ID:** Kd 7
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Kathinakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathinakkhandhaka* is the seventh chapter of the Mahāvagga within the Khandhaka section of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983]. Often translated as "The chapter on the robe-making ceremony" or "On kathina" [Norman 1983], it sets forth the legal procedures and monastic regulations governing the *kaṭhina* cloth-offering and robe-making ceremony, which takes place during the last month of the rainy season after the completion of the *vassa* residence. Performance of the ceremony extends monks' robe privileges until the end of the cold season, and the majority of the text provides an intricate, technical legal analysis of the conditions that either terminate or maintain those privileges [von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983].

 In modern Southeast Asian history, modernist Cambodian reform monks including Chuon Nath and Huot Tath produced an abbreviated Khmer translation of the *Kathinakkhandhaka* under the auspices of the Buddhist Institute to standardize monastic conduct [Hansen 2007].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd8 Kathinavastu; xct-mu-kd8 Kaṭhina; lzh-mu-kd8 Kaṭhina; Lzh Sarv Kd8 Kaṭhina Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 8 Kaṭhina Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 8 Kaṭhina Khandhaka
- Passage-level parallels: SN 15.13 Tiṁsamattasutta
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn4 Vagga 4. Uposatha

**Sources**

- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pali Literature (1996) — Position of the Kathinakkhandhaka in the Khandhaka framework and its characterization as technical legal material.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (1983) — English title rendering, sequence within Khandhaka, and assessment of textual obscurities.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvāstivāda Literature (1979) — Close correspondence between the Pali Kathinakkhandhaka and northern Kathinavastu texts regarding origins and robe rules.
- [Dutt] Nalinaksha Dutt, Early History of the Spread of Buddhism and the Buddhist Schools — Correspondence between the Kathinakkhandhaka and chapters of the Tibetan Dulva.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, A Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Information on translations by Rhys Davids & Oldenberg and I. B. Horner.
- [Hansen 2007] Anne Ruth Hansen, How to Behave: Buddhism and Modernity in Colonial Cambodia (2007) — Modern vernacular translation of Kathinakkhandhaka by modernist Cambodian monks.
